blockers: Reported ground-anchor drift is 1.0px, while the sprite contract requires exactly 0px drift at anchor (96,176) across every frame.
The locomotion cycles lack convincing weight transfer: the torso remains largely rigid while the legs swing beneath it, creating a mannequin-like and intermittently ice-skating read.

Foot planting is not sufficiently explicit. Narrow, nearly straight lower limbs and ambiguous heel-toe contacts make the planted foot difficult to identify, while sword tips sometimes compete visually with the ground contact.
The signature gesture is primarily a blade arc. The sword changes position without enough visible arm extension, shoulder participation, torso anticipation, controlled overshoot, or settle.
The idle strip is effectively static at native scale. Breathing, garment response, hair, collar, and brass elements do not produce a readable contained-life cycle.
At native 1x, the face, high collar, corset, hands, and weapon grip collapse into a generic blue vertical figure. The intended costume hierarchy is not reliably legible without magnification.

The front silhouette is too narrow and mechanically symmetrical, with weak separation between arms, torso, thighs, and hip equipment. The character reads more as a rigid mannequin than a deliberate rapier specialist.

The 8-direction set appears to reuse a largely generic walk solution across views instead of giving each direction coherent hip rotation, shoulder counter-rotation, perspective compression, and direction-specific weight.
high_value_changes: Rebuild the walk cycle from a locked root and explicit contact keys: solve the planted foot at Y=176 first, then animate center-of-mass travel, knee compression, heel-toe roll, hip rotation, and shoulder counter-rotation.
Redesign the front silhouette with a clearer shoulder-to-corset taper, separated forearms and thighs, and an unmistakable hand-hilt-scabbard relationship.

Simplify the native 1x material palette into deliberate value blocks: separate dark hair from the navy costume on dark backgrounds, strengthen the brass into a readable gold accent, and reserve bright white for structural costume planes and the rapier.
Reconstruct the face as a small set of intentional stylized planes rather than a pale rectangular mask with isolated cyan eye pixels and a tiny mouth.

Reanimate the signature gesture as a full-body controlled flourish: add a restrained anticipation, hand and shoulder lead, torso follow-through, planted-base counterbalance, blade overshoot, and a visible settle.
Add restrained secondary motion to the hair, collar, coat edges, brass attachments, and scabbard, with overlap and delayed settling rather than uniform rigid movement.
Make the eight directions genuinely directional instead of mirrored variants by adjusting visible shoulder width, torso twist, leg overlap, weapon foreshortening, and back-view silhouette.
optional_notes: Standing height is compliant at approximately 113.8px, so the scale ceiling is not the current problem.

The light blue, white, and brass accents provide usable separation on a light background, but the dark-background native inspection exposes insufficient separation within the navy and obsidian materials.
No previous-round comparison sheet was supplied, so visual regressions from the prior iteration cannot be independently verified.
strongest_improvements: The candidate stays below the 128px standing-height limit.
The rapier provides a potentially useful directional identity in side and diagonal views.
The explicit 8-direction and signature-gesture coverage gives a workable animation framework, but the key poses require a substantial weight and anatomy pass.
luna_evaluation.single_most_important_next_change: Rebuild every locomotion key around an exactly root-locked planted foot at Y=176 and a visible center-of-mass transfer; do not polish the blade gesture or secondary motion until the feet, hips, and shoulders carry believable weight.
